items.detail: The drift lower became a second straight decline on Tuesday: the **S&P 500 fell 24.91 points (-0.3%) to 7,728.20**, the **Nasdaq dropped 159.91 points (-0.6%) to 26,445.45** and the **Dow lost 184.13 points to 53,791.85**, leaving the index two sessions removed from last week's record high.
items.why: The US-Iran standoff hardened rather than eased, with Trump rebuking Tehran's demand for war reparations and saying he would wait for economic pressure to build, so traders pared risk into Wednesday's CPI rather than chase the record.

items.detail: The AI-capex funding worry rotated from Intel to Alphabet, which **sank 3.61%** to lead megacap losses after closing a **$25 billion senior notes offering** on Aug 10 and guiding 2026 capital expenditure to **$195-205 billion**, with quarterly capex doubling year-on-year to $44.9 billion.
items.why: Alphabet's data-centre buildout has pushed free cash flow negative for the first time and is now being funded with debt, extending the same dilution-and-leverage anxiety that hit Intel's $15 billion share sale a day earlier across the AI complex.

items.detail: Crude extended its climb rather than mean-reverting: **Brent hovered near $89** and **WTI settled around $83**, up again from Monday's $87.72 and $82.13, taking oil to roughly a three-month high.
items.why: Iran reiterated it will keep the Strait of Hormuz shut until its demands are met, removing the near-term reopening premium traders had priced and leaving the supply disruption open-ended.

items.detail: September hike odds have swung dovish into the print: one read now puts the probability of a **September hike at 46%, down from 67% a week earlier**, while **Polymarket prices just 36%** for a 25bp move versus 63% for no change — a shift from Monday's 50-50 CME FedWatch split.
items.why: Last Friday's weak payrolls continue to dominate the rate path, and traders judge that an oil-driven energy spike arriving after the July survey period will not by itself force the Fed's hand next month.

items.detail: July CPI lands **Wednesday at 8:30am ET**, with consensus at **+0.1% m/m (3.4% y/y)** headline and **+0.2% m/m (2.5% y/y)** core, though Kalshi traders lean lower at **3.3%** — followed by July retail sales on Friday, Aug 14.
items.why: The July data predates the current crude spike, so the print is being read less as a verdict on today's oil shock than as the last clean inflation reading before it feeds through.

items.detail: Monday's flat hold gave way to an outright decline: the **Nifty 50 lost 112.10 points (-0.46%) to 24,471.70**, closing below 24,500, while the **Sensex fell 388.19 points (-0.49%) to 78,154.25** and **Bank Nifty dropped 240.70 points (-0.42%) to 57,446.25**.
items.why: Crude's push toward $90 a barrel combined with renewed weakness in financials and a softer rupee, turning the previous session's crude-versus-earnings standoff decisively in favour of the energy headwind.

items.detail: Sector leadership flipped from Monday's realty-led tape to defensives: **pharma and IT outperformed** while **FMCG, realty and metals lagged**, with **Dr Reddy's Laboratories rising 4.06% to ₹1,205.80** and Eternal adding 2.03% to ₹316.55 ahead of TCS.
items.why: With crude and the currency both moving against domestic cyclicals, investors rotated into dollar-earning exporters like pharma and IT, which benefit from a weaker rupee rather than being squeezed by it.

items.detail: The currency has now joined crude as a drag — the **rupee closed near ₹95.44 per dollar, down 14 paise**, as Brent pushed toward the **$90** mark from Monday's $87.72.
items.why: A sustained crude bid directly widens India's import bill for a country sourcing over 85% of its oil abroad, and the rupee is absorbing that deterioration in the trade math, compounding the inflation impulse rather than cushioning it.

items.detail: India's own July CPI is due **today, Aug 12**, with a Reuters poll of 40 economists at **4.50%** (up from June's 4.38%) and a Mint poll of 18 at an unchanged **4.4%** — a second straight month above the RBI's 4% target, with forecasts spanning 3.96% to 5.50%.
items.why: Higher food prices account for most of the expected upward pressure, and a second consecutive overshoot of the RBI's medium-term target narrows the room for policy support just as external cost pressure builds.

items.detail: Flows turned marginally supportive but thin: **FPIs bought ₹258.55 crore** and **DIIs ₹24.77 crore** on Aug 11, and **GIFT Nifty at roughly 24,550.5** — a 10-point premium — points to a flat open, with the **78,000-77,800 Sensex zone** flagged as the level that must hold.
items.why: Foreign buying returned in modest size after recent selling, but position sizes stayed small with both the Indian and US CPI prints landing on the same day.

items.detail: Bitcoin's slide extended a third session, **dipping 0.7% to about $63,394** after a morning push to $64,400 failed, while **Ether fell 2.8% to roughly $1,874** — a fresh break below the $1,900 level it was defending on Monday.
items.why: A failed intraday rally triggered $34.4 million in long liquidations, and Bitfinex points to 1.79 million BTC of overhead supply pinning the market in a $62,000-$65,000 band with no catalyst to break it before CPI.

items.detail: The ETF bid — the tape's one unambiguous positive in Monday's brief — has broken: US spot bitcoin ETFs **shed $144.67 million**, ending a five-session streak that had drawn **$853.5 million**, with **BlackRock's IBIT alone losing $53.56 million** alongside Grayscale's GBTC.
items.why: The first net-outflow day of August removes the structural buyer that had been absorbing spot weakness, meaning institutional flows have stopped decoupling from price and are now confirming it.

items.detail: BlackRock cut IBIT's **in-kind conversion minimum from $25 million to $1 million — a 96% reduction**, and has signalled it intends to push the threshold lower still, ultimately toward any transaction size.
items.why: Holders of appreciated bitcoin can now swap into IBIT shares without triggering a taxable cash sale at a threshold reachable by RIAs and family offices rather than only Wall Street desks, widening the pool of potential converters.

items.detail: The CLARITY Act's path is now concrete rather than merely delayed: Majority Leader Thune filed cloture before recess, setting a **first procedural vote for Sept 15** that still requires **60 votes**, while **Galaxy Research cut 2026 passage odds from 50% to 30%** and Polymarket prices roughly 17%.
items.why: Democrats are holding out for ethics, conflict-of-interest and illicit-finance safeguards that Republicans have not conceded, so scheduling a vote has not closed the nine-vote gap that stopped the bill in August.

items.detail: Institutional demand is fragmenting across assets rather than moving as one bloc: on the same day bitcoin funds bled $144.67 million, **Solana products drew $8.83 million of inflows** while **ether funds lost $14.59 million**.
items.why: Allocators are differentiating between crypto assets instead of treating the sector as a single risk trade, which is why SOL held up as BTC and ETH flows turned negative together.

crossCuttingTheme: The Hormuz closure has hardened from a negotiation to a siege — Iran reaffirming the strait stays shut and Trump opting to let economic pressure build pushed Brent to nearly $90, and that open-ended supply shock is now compounding rather than triggering: it drove the S&P 500's second straight loss while AI-capex funding fears rotated from Intel to Alphabet, knocked the Nifty below 24,500 by dragging the rupee to ₹95.44 and worsening India's import math into its own 4.4-4.5% CPI print, and coincided with the break in bitcoin's five-day ETF inflow streak that had been the only thing holding BTC above $63,400 — with Wednesday's US July CPI, which predates the spike entirely, arriving as a backward-looking reading into a forward-looking energy problem.
